$comment: Fleet registry for the /orchestrate skill. Committed: the fleet shape is a project fact.
Secrets never live here. SSH uses key auth resolved by the OS agent; no passwords, no
connection strings. 'repo' is that machine's checkout path, not this machine's.
Paths use forward slashes - .NET, pwsh, and git all accept them on Windows, and it keeps
this file free of backslash-escaping bugs.
Hostnames do NOT indicate form factor. Windows auto-names most PCs DESKTOP-XXXXXXX;
box3 reports DESKTOP-F5LK8MA but is physically a laptop (PCSystemType=Mobile, internal
battery). Recorded here so nobody re-derives it from the name and gets it wrong.
The fleet is TWO LAPTOPS. box2 (DESKTOP-G83CCSH) was retired 2026-08-23 - see the
'box2, retired' section of .claude/fleet/mission.md for why and for what was learned on
it, so none of that is paid for twice if a desktop ever rejoins.
transport:
local  - same machine as the orchestrator. Bash/pwsh directly.
ssh    - headless or `ssh -t` for a visible tab. Full control: model, effort, start, stop.
rc     - Remote Control. Driven with SendMessage, not a shell; ONE verb only (prompt),
so model and effort cannot be set. NO MACHINE USES rc NOW. box3 keeps an
rcSessionName only as a manual fallback if its ssh transport ever breaks;
the name changes on every session restart, so confirm with ListAgents first.
maxConcurrent is a CEILING, not a target. How many workers actually run on a box, and at
which model and effort, is the orchestrator's decision per mission - see /orchestrate section 2.
enabled:false means the transport is declared but not yet provisioned. /orchestrate must
refuse to dispatch to it and say which setup step is missing - never silently fall back.

machines.notes: Orchestrator host. The ONLY machine with XAMPP/MariaDB 10.4.32, so every card touching the database, a migration, or the running API belongs here (ADR-013 pins the three DB identities to this host). Held to 2 concurrent workers: this box is also running the orchestrator session and the user's Visual Studio.

machines.clockTz: Singapore Standard Time - matches box1. Was Pacific until 2026-08-23; see notes.
machines.notes: THE worker box. Sole secondary since box2 was retired 2026-08-23, so it is no longer scoped to documentations/ - it takes EVERY card that does not need MariaDB. SSH TRANSPORT LIVE, proven end to end 2026-08-23 (SMOKE-02, haiku/low, $0.069). Addressed as the ssh_config Host alias `box3`; user, identity file and hostname live in box1's ~/.ssh/config, not here. Key-only auth, PasswordAuthentication no, sshd firewall rule scoped to 192.168.100.0/24 - the subnet, not a single IP, because DHCP will move box1 eventually and a rule pinned to one lease fails silently later. Store/MSIX pwsh resolves fine under a non-interactive SSH login. PCSystemType=2 (Mobile) - a LAPTOP despite the DESKTOP- hostname; read formFactor from here, never from the name. Exists away from home: both fleet boxes are laptops on the same hotspot, so the fleet is whole at school. 57.8 GB free is the tightest constraint on it - place disk-heavy work on box1 and check free space before dispatching four at once. CLOCK: FIXED 2026-08-23 - the user ran Set-TimeZone -Id 'Singapore Standard Time' on this box, so both machines now sit at UTC+8 and their wall clocks agree to within 2 seconds. It was Pacific before that, ~15 hours out, which would have put a wrong LOCAL timestamp into any evidence file, document or test expectation a box3 worker wrote. UTC always agreed, so the DATETIME(6)-in-UTC rule was never at risk - the hazard was display time only. Kept here because a reinstalled Windows defaults back to the installer's zone and reopens it silently: re-check with (Get-TimeZone).Id if a box3 timestamp ever looks wrong.

$effortNote: high, NOT medium. Corrected 2026-08-23 against Anthropic's documented guidance after
the user asked what the original table was based on - the honest answer was nothing.
The documented rule: minimum high for intelligence-sensitive work, high/xhigh for
long-horizon agentic tasks, max when correctness matters more than cost, low for
simple sub-tasks. xhigh is Claude Code's OWN default, so a fleet on medium was running
below what Claude Code would have chosen for itself.
Effort levels are low/medium/high/xhigh/max - verified against `claude --help` on this
haiku is deliberately NOT the default and should not be reintroduced as a cost saving:
effort is unsupported on Haiku 4.5, so haiku/low reads as a tuning choice while the
effort flag does nothing; its context is 200K against 1M for Opus 5 and Sonnet 5; and
Sonnet 5 is $3/$15 per MTok against Haiku's $1/$5, two to three times, not ten.
$ceilingNote: Every limit in this file is EXTERNAL and invisible to the worker. That is the user's
explicit design decision, 2026-08-23: a model told it is running out of something
paces itself, consolidates early and settles for the first adequate answer, which is a
quality loss bought with an unmeasured saving. Efficiency comes from architecture
(separate context windows, reports not transcripts, tight briefs) and from placement
(model/effort per card) - never from telling a model to be frugal. Nothing here may
ever be written into a brief.
maxBudgetUsd: a hard spend cut-off, -Mode bg ONLY - `--max-budget-usd` requires
`--print`, so it does nothing in the tty mode that is now the default. It kills the
session from outside; fleet.ps1 surfaces it as BUDGET EXCEEDED.
timeoutMinutes: enforced two ways. With -Wait, by the dispatcher. Without it, by a
watchdog process started alongside the worker, which kills the run at the deadline
ONLY IF it has produced no report - so a runaway is bounded while a finished tty
worker whose tab is still being read is left alone. Before this existed an async
dispatch had no enforced ceiling of any kind.
$permissionModeNote: bypassPermissions, and this was the USER'S EXPLICIT DECISION on 2026-08-23. It is not a
default that drifted in - do not quietly lower it, and do not re-ask per dispatch.
Why the two milder modes do not work here, both measured on box3, not assumed:
acceptEdits auto-accepts file EDITS ONLY and still prompts on every Bash/PowerShell
call. SMOKE-03 sat at flat CPU for 15 minutes holding a fleet slot.
auto did the same. On Windows it cannot sandbox a shell call, so it falls back to
prompting. SMOKE-04 stalled identically with hasTrustDialogAccepted=true and an
empty allowedTools, which is what proves it was the permission prompt and not a
This is a PERMISSION-MODE property, not a model one. The first reading was 'haiku cannot
run unattended'; that is wrong, opus stalls in exactly the same place.
What still guards a worker, so this is narrower than it sounds:
- The L1-L3 Claude Code hooks fire regardless of permission mode. block-csharp still
blocks a .cs write, check-vbproj still enforces G-B/G-D, stop-guardrails still runs.
- The L4 pre-commit hook is installed on every worker clone by bootstrap-worker-machine.
- Workers commit locally and NEVER push. Integration is the orchestrator's, in one place.
- Both boxes are the user's own machines on a private LAN.
The residual risk is real and accepted: a worker can run any command on its own box.
